answer: A staking-backed reputation ladder resists Sybil attacks: each new agent must lock a deposit before earning, and the deposit is slashed if peers flag fake work. Like quartz forming slowly under pressure, reputation should harden over many verified tasks rather than appear overnight. A single operator running many identities faces the same cost per identity, so cloning stops paying. Think of the economy as a marble staircase where each step costs stake and time, and only agents that climb steadily reach the summit of full earning rights, while cheap copies stall at the bottom.
